title: Highlight the Shortest Unique Substring
prompt:
Implement `highlight_unique_substrings(words)`. For each nonempty lowercase or mixed-case ASCII word, wrap its shortest nonempty contiguous substring that appears in none of the other words in square brackets. Compare substrings case-insensitively; repeated occurrences within the same word do not disqualify a substring. If several qualifying substrings have the same minimum length, choose the one with the earliest start position. Preserve the original spelling and case in the output.

Return one highlighted string per input word in the same order. The input list may be empty. Assume no word is wholly contained case-insensitively in another word, so each word has a qualifying substring.

example.reasoning: The single letters 'a', 'b', and 'c' occur in both words. The shortest substring unique to each word is its final letter.

background_note: Consolidates the 2022 report's shortest-unique-substring task and case-insensitive matching with the 2025 report's square-bracket annotation format. Earliest-start tie-breaking is a deterministic local convention; the 2025 report does not establish a shortest-substring requirement. A later public Staff SWE report independently specifies shortest, case-insensitive matching, original case/order, and first-position ties, using underline tags rather than this exercise's brackets. It corroborates the practice convention without establishing the 2025 MLE wording.
